guide.summary: Forgejo documents OAuth2 provider support for third-party apps with user consent, but OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented and apps obtaining tokens have administrative rights. Repository listing is documented via the repo search endpoint with pagination, yet no OAuth permission identifier for read-only repository access is documented. Register a test app on a test instance, run the authorization flow, and verify granted access before any production decision.

findings.title: Forgejo documents OAuth2 provider support for third-party apps
findings.detail: Forgejo can act as an OAuth2 provider for third-party apps with the user's consent. This applies to individual customer accounts on their own instances.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 provider Forgejo supports acting as an OAuth2 provider to allow third party applications to access its resources with the user’s consent.

findings.title: OAuth apps are registered on the instance admin page
findings.detail: Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider, and OAuth2 applications must be created on the instance's /admin/applications page. Each customer instance needs an administrator to register the app.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer instance where the app is installed

evidence.quote: Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider. To achieve that, OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page.

findings.title: Authorized apps may receive administrative rights
findings.detail: Third-party apps that obtain a token through an OAuth2 application have administrative rights. This conflicts with a read-only least-privilege goal and must be resolved before rollout.

evidence.quote: Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.

findings.title: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented
findings.detail: OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so the documented token scopes cannot be requested per app. Scoped access tokens are a separate mechanism from OAuth2.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.
Note Scoped tokens or personal access tokens are entirely different from OAuth2;

findings.title: Repository listing pagination is documented on the search endpoint
findings.detail: The API supports page and limit parameters, with Link and x-total-count headers. The repo search endpoint is documented with a limit example.

evidence.quote: Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
curl -v "https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/repos/search?limit=1" ...

steps.title: Register OAuth app on a test Forgejo instance
steps.detail: Create an OAuth2 application on the test instance's admin applications page and record the client ID and secret. Leave other fields at defaults and record the redirect URI.
steps.doneWhen: The OAuth app appears in the admin applications list with a client ID and redirect URI recorded.

evidence.quote: Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider. To achieve that, OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page.
Leave all other fields at their default values.
It will show in the list of authentication sources at https://forgejo.example.com/admin/auths .

steps.appliesWhen: Test instance where the developer is an administrator

steps.title: Implement authorize and token exchange callback
steps.detail: Build the authorize redirect with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and state, plus the code-to-token exchange. The exchange POST must use the same redirect URI as the authorize request.
steps.doneWhen: The app builds an authorize URL and posts the code exchange with a matching redirect URI in a local test.

evidence.quote: https://[ YOUR-FORGEJO-URL ]/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&state=STATE The CLIENT_ID can be obtained by registering an application in the settings. The STATE is a random string that will be

https://[ REDIRECT_URI ]?code=RETURNED_CODE&state=STATE Using the provided code from the redirect, you can request a new application and refresh token. The access token endpoint accepts POST requests with application/json and
The REDIRECT_URI in the access_token request must match the REDIRECT_URI in the authorize request.

steps.title: Authorize representative test account
steps.detail: Sign in as a representative test account on the test instance and complete the consent flow. Record the access token returned by the exchange and inspect the granted access shown during consent.
steps.doneWhen: An access token is obtained through the callback and the granted access is recorded.

evidence.quote: Redirect the user to the authorization endpoint in order to get their consent for accessing the resources:
The user will now be asked to authorize your application. If they authorize it, the user will be redirected to the REDIRECT_URL , for example:
Use the access_token to make API requests to access the user’s resources.

steps.appliesWhen: Test account on a test instance

steps.title: Resolve visible repository listing
steps.detail: No documented endpoint lists all repositories visible to the connected person. The owned-repositories endpoint is narrower than the requested action, and no visible-repository listing is documented for OAuth access. Leave the request empty and confirm the documented listing scope with the provider before implementing. Read-only use only: do not create, edit or delete repositories.
steps.doneWhen: A documented endpoint is confirmed that lists repositories visible to the authenticated person and supports page and limit pagination, with a read-only boundary check that performs no write requests.

evidence.quote: Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
GET /api/v1/user/repos | List the repos that the authenticated user owns
OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.

steps.title: Verify read-only boundary using granted access and request log
steps.detail: Inspect the granted access for the token and the outgoing request log for the test. Do not send any write request to prove the boundary. Boundary check: confirm no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE requests were sent and the granted access matches the read need.
steps.doneWhen: The request log shows only GET requests and the granted access has been recorded.

evidence.quote: read : GET routes
write : POST , PUT , PATCH , and DELETE routes (in addition to GET )

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Register OAuth app on a test Forgejo instance
Create an OAuth2 application on the test instance's admin applications page and record the client ID and secret. Leave other fields at defaults and record the redirect URI.
Fields: Instance base URL, Client ID, Client secret, Redirect URI

Implement authorize and token exchange callback
Build the authorize redirect with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and state, plus the code-to-token exchange. The exchange POST must use the same redirect URI as the authorize request.
Fields: Redirect URI, Client ID, Client secret

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Authorize representative test account
Done when: An access token is obtained through the callback and the granted access is recorded.

Resolve visible repository listing
Done when: A documented endpoint is confirmed that lists repositories visible to the authenticated person and supports page and limit pagination, with a read-only boundary check that performs no write requests.

Verify read-only boundary using granted access and request log
Done when: The request log shows only GET requests and the granted access has been recorded.
